svg.title: Single passive binary delay lattice and shared-pump timing
svg.desc: Six balanced two-path stages implement a 64-tap uniform field impulse response. Stage delays are 10, 20, 40, 80, 160 and 320 picoseconds, corresponding to 1.5, 3, 6, 12, 24 and 48 millimeters at group index two. Total differential waveguide length is 94.5 millimeters. Each 32-slot coefficient burst lasts 320 picoseconds and is followed by a 320 picosecond blank b_m interval. Frame starts are separated by 640 picoseconds. Frame zero has a full plateau from 310 to 640 picoseconds and an accepted window from 320 to 640 picoseconds. The next reader b_m sequence follows this valid window plus propagation latency. The raw lattice output remains connected and contains unaccepted transients; it is not selected by a shutter. All delays and pump edges are ideal, and the 1.5625 gigahertz reader frame rate is not a neural-network token rate.

g.text: Single binary delay lattice · ideal shared-pump timing
Six balanced two-way cells; one permanent optical path through the accumulator; perfect phase and delay
D delays the optical field by τ = 10 ps. Static path phases align the selected output port at every stage.
Total: 6 cells · 12 couplers · 630 ps differential delay · 94.5 mm at n_g = 2. Unused coupler ports are terminated.
ONE FRAME EVERY 640 ps · bₘ DOES THE OPTICAL ACCEPTANCE
R = 32 terms · 320 ps generation burst · 320 ps blank burst interval · common propagation latency omitted
Frame 0: full plateau [310, 640) ps; accept [320, 640) ps. Later accepted windows repeat every 640 ps.
Unaccepted intervals can contain rising sums, old tails and overlap. The raw optical path remains connected.
The next reader adds its link + core latency to the bₘ schedule; only its DFG 2 terms enter the next sum.
32 active slots + 32 zero slots isolate successive sums.
Each accepted 32-slot window contains Σ zₘ / 64.
Generation may overlap an older tail inside the lattice.
Only completed windows are converted by the next reader.
At 320 ps frame spacing, a single lattice mixes frames.
No EO input router, output selector, or output shutter.
This is not the complete recurrent-model token rate.
Pump edges, delay, loss balance and carrier phase are ideal.
Figures 10–11 retain a separate engineering alternative.
Differential lengths exclude common paths, bends and routing. Engineering margins and finite pump extinction require separate validation.
